verification_report.summary: Checked all twelve proofs and the curvewise definition in textual order, and checked the external references through arXiv theorem search followed by primary-source lookup. The curve envelopes, normalization descent, affine tube argument, conditional scalar upgrade, nonopenness example, and defect inequalities are sound. The full submitted proof fails the strict criterion because the final corollary loses a smoothness hypothesis and the retraction theorem invokes missing internal dependencies. Both defects are repairable; this verdict does not assert that the stated conclusions are false.

critical_errors.location: cor:p031-scalar-defect-curve-witness, replacement of C_0 by a connected affinoid neighborhood
critical_errors.issue: The restricted affinoid curve need not be smooth in the convention used by the cited curve-test theorem and the preceding localization theorem. Gubler–Rabinoff §2.13 defines smooth as rig-smooth and boundaryless, whereas a nonempty affinoid curve has relative boundary equal to its nonempty Shilov boundary (§3.1(3)). Thus the application of thm:p031-curvewise-scalar-defect-localization to the replacement curve does not meet its smoothness hypothesis. The local-failure assertion can be preserved by passing instead to a connected open neighborhood inside the affinoid interior. This is a repairable theorem-application error, not a counterexample to the witness statement. Source: [Gubler–Rabinoff](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13548v2).

gaps.location: thm:p031-canonical-scalar-retraction-normal-form, construction of sigma and the two identities used for the fibre maximum
gaps.issue: The proof relies on cor:p031-canonical-scalar-section-anchor, eq:p031-canonical-scalar-section-regularization, and eq:p031-scalar-fiber-maximum, none of which is stated or proved in the supplied text or resolved to an external reference there. These are missing dependencies for the submitted standalone proof, and the later canonical-retraction formulations inherit this omission. The existence claim is independently supported by Poineau, Corollaries 3.7 and 3.14 and Remark 3.13, and the identities follow directly from continuity of a section, so this is a completeness gap rather than evidence that the normal form is false. Source: [Poineau](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1105.0250).

repair_hints: In the final corollary, retain the original test curve C_0, which is already separated under the cited GR convention, or choose an affinoid neighborhood A of c and then use the connected component of Int(A) containing c. This preserves smoothness and local failure. For the retraction theorem, supply the three missing internal references or cite Poineau, Corollaries 3.7 and 3.14 with Remark 3.13, for the continuous section and prove the identities directly: b=(a∘π)^* satisfies a∘π≤b≤a*∘π; continuity of σ makes b∘σ an upper-semicontinuous majorant of a, hence a*≤b∘σ≤a*. Therefore b(σ(x))=a*(x), which is the maximum of b on the fibre. The remaining retraction and localization deductions then apply.
